catalog_quote: Ivie has two contrastive tones, high tone (´) and low tone . The language is also characterized by features of automatic downstep, upstep, and downdrift. Automatic upstep which is phonologically predictable is analyzed as an allotone of high tone. The syllable is the tone bearing unit in Ivie. Tone performs both lexical and grammatical functions in the language but its function at the level of grammar is more complex. In nouns, minimal pairs contrasting high and low tones are attested as shown in the examples in (2.4). A change in tone brings about a change in meaning and new lexical items are created in this way. (p.38) ... The overall structure of Ivie syllables is consonant-vowel (CV). The onset is obligatory for verbs, but those of the initial syllables of nouns are onsetless. Consonant clusters are not normally attested. Each syllable bears one of two tones: high or low. ... The ph…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ivie (North Ibie, Okpekpe dialect) is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with downstep, upstep and downdrift; every CV syllable carries H or L, nouns show lexical tone minimal pairs, verbs get tense/aspect tone melodies; the phonological word is defined as the domain of the tone pattern. The description says nothing about word stress or accent anywhere (full-thesis scanned searched).
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal details: HH disyllabic nouns realised H!H; contour tones only as phonologically conditioned combinations on a short syllable after glide formation.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone pattern domain = phonological/prosodic word (usually = grammatical word, larger in compounds and verb complexes); elision domain = phonological clause; pause group = sentence. No stress domain given because no stress is described.
new_statements.identity_note: All four opened sources describe Ivie = 'North Ibie' (Glottolog dialect Ivbie North [ivbi1242] of the ivbi1241 cluster), specifically the Okpekpe variety spoken by the Masagbors; nothing was found for the Okpela [okpe1248] or Arhe/Ate [arhe1238] members of the cluster.

sources.note: Nothing on stress in Ivie (the only 'stress'/'accent' tokens are in the general clitic literature review on Polish/West Flemish etc.). Sec. 2.1.3 'Basic tone system' (p.38): two contrastive tones H and L, automatic downstep, upstep, downdrift; syllable is the TBU; lexical minimal pairs in nouns, verbs toneless underlyingly with tense/aspect tone melodies; tonal morphemes. Sec. 2.1.4.2-3 (p.42): CV syllables, each syllable bears H or L; 'the phonological word is.. the unit bearing the tone pattern'.
